bookTitle: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis

facts.statement: Volume Price Analysis (VPA) combines the only two leading indicators in trading: price and volume. In isolation each is weak, but combined they act like gunpowder—an explosive combination where price reveals buying or selling while volume validates whether the move is genuine or false.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: There are only two leading indicators in trading. One is price, the other is volume. In isolation, they are weak and reveal little, but put them together, and just like gunpowder, they become an explosive combination.

facts.statement: Volume Price Analysis is a 100-year-old analytical methodology used by iconic trading pioneers Charles Dow, Jesse Livermore, and Richard Wyckoff, who amassed huge fortunes analyzing price and volume using only the ticker tape, pencil, and paper.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: This was the approach used by the iconic traders of the past, such as Charles Dow, Jesse Livermore, and Richard Wyckoff. These traders built huge fortunes using this technique, using nothing more than the ticker tape, pencil and paper.

facts.statement: VPA applies universally across all financial markets—including equities, indices, futures, commodities, bonds, and spot forex—and across every timeframe from 1-minute tick charts to monthly charts, provided price and volume appear on the same chart.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: It can be applied to all markets in all time frames, and can be used to trade all instruments... The only proviso is that we have price and volume on the same chart.

facts.statement: In January 1998, after reading a Sunday Times article, Anna Coulling attended a seminar hosted by trader Albert Labos aboard the HMS President (a 1918 anti-submarine Q-ship on the Thames), paying £5,000 for a two-week course on volume trading alongside her husband David.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Two weeks later, on an early Sunday morning, I joined hundreds of other hopefuls in a packed room, on the HMS President... First, Albert exhorted the 'spies' in the room to leave.

facts.statement: At the HMS President seminar, Labos introduced Tom Williams, a partially sighted ex-syndicate trader. A syndicate trader operates within an institutional capital pool to quietly accumulate or distribute large stock blocks without prematurely disrupting market prices.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: We were then introduced to a Tom Williams. We were told that Tom was partially sighted, and I can’t quite remember if he had a white cane. We were also told that he was an ex 'syndicate trader'.

facts.statement: Because all financial markets are manipulated by market makers and institutional syndicates, individual retail traders cannot fight them head-on; instead, traders must read volume footprints to buy when insiders accumulate and sell when insiders distribute.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Throughout the two weeks, the over-riding message was that all financial markets are manipulated in one way or another. And the only way to know whether a price move was genuine or false was by using volume.

facts.statement: Published in 1923 as a disguised biography of Jesse Livermore, Edwin Lefevre's Reminiscences of a Stock Operator established that nothing is new on Wall Street because human emotions of fear and greed never change, causing price-volume patterns to repeat endlessly.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: There is nothing new in Wall Street. There can't be because speculation is as old as the hills. Whatever happens in the stock market today has happened before and will happen again.

facts.statement: While specialists and market makers can easily manipulate price quotes, stage fake breakout spikes, and exploit news events, they cannot hide volume because accumulating or liquidating massive institutional inventories inevitably leaves transparent transaction spikes on the chart.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: And the only way to know whether a price move was genuine or false was by using volume. Volume cannot be hidden. It is there for everyone to see.

facts.statement: Market makers act like Uncle Joe running Widgets & Co.: when his warehouse is full, he spreads shortage rumors to sell inventory at high retail prices (distribution); when empty, he triggers panic selling to replenish inventory at cheap wholesale prices (accumulation).

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Market makers function exactly like wholesale merchants. Uncle Joe owns a widget distribution warehouse... selling at retail rates (distribution phase) and buying back widgets at wholesale prices (accumulation phase).

facts.statement: Price without volume is like an empty, rainy provincial auction room where an item sells on one low bid, whereas high volume is a packed summer auction driving fierce bidding; similarly, volume acts like a hosepipe sprinkler valve regulating price pressure.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: A price chart without volume is like an auction taking place in an empty, rainy provincial room... Water flowing through a pipe represents price movement, while the sprinkler valve represents volume.

facts.statement: As documented by Richard Ney, on November 22, 1963, specialists used President Kennedy's assassination panic to mark AT&T down from $138 to $130, absorbed retail panic selling at wholesale, closed the exchange, and reopened on November 25 at $140.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Specialists used the panic surrounding President Kennedy's assassination as an alibi to drop stock prices to wholesale levels (e.g., AT&T was marked down from $138 to $130)... and reopened AT&T on November 25 at $140.

facts.statement: Under Wyckoff's Law of Effort versus Result, volume effort must match price spread result. Validation occurs when a wide price spread is backed by high volume, or when a narrow price spread is accompanied by low volume.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Price spread (the result) must be proportional to volume (the effort). Validation: Wide price spread + high volume, or narrow price spread + low volume.

facts.statement: A VPA anomaly occurs when effort and result diverge: a wide price spread on low volume warns of a fake move or market-maker trap, while a narrow price spread on high volume signals heavy insider absorption and an impending reversal.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Anomaly: Wide price spread + low volume (fake move/trap), or narrow price spread + high volume (insider absorption/reversal warning).

facts.statement: Volume is never judged as an isolated absolute number; traders must always evaluate each volume bar relative to preceding volume bars on the exact same chart and data feed to judge whether activity is high, average, or low.

sourceCitation.book: A Complete Guide To Volume Price Analysis
sourceCitation.excerpt: Volume bars should only be evaluated relative to preceding volume bars on the same data feed.

generalAssumptions: Market price manipulation is structurally transparent on the volume tape.
Effort versus result governs institutional capital movement.
